description:
Refunds full/partial, exchanges with price-difference settlement, transfers and controlled resale, event-cancellation bulk flows — all as compensating journal entries (ADR-003).

**Conditions of Success:**
- Refund/exchange restore inventory and write compensating entries; chain still verifies
- Exchanges settle price differences in either direction
- Cancellation flow processes an event's full order book with per-order outcomes

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

Decomposed 2026-07-31 into **four stories** (TKT-156 → TKT-159) plus one deliberate
carve-out (TKT-160).

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Quality gates extracted | ✅ | `make check`, contract/OpenAPI drift, organizer scoping, integer minor units — appended to every child |
| Vertical slices | ✅ | Each child is money → journal → inventory/tickets end to end, demoable on its own. None is a layer. |
| Sizing | ⚠️ | TKT-158 (exchange) is the largest — a reversal and a sale in one operation across four services. Flagged, not split: the atomicity AC is the ticket, and splitting it would produce two halves neither of which can be verified alone. |
| Prefactoring split out first | ✅ | TKT-156 *is* the prefactor: it builds the refund primitive that TKT-158 and TKT-159 both call. |
| Dependency order | ✅ | 156 → 157 → {158, 159}. No forward dependencies. Cycle check walked: none. |
| AC verifiable | ✅ | Every AC names an observable outcome and, where the risk is a race, the test that must exist. |
| Links + cycle check | ✅ | `blocks`/`blocked-by` wired; TKT-160 blocked-by TKT-21. |
| Context-mémo baked | ✅ | Per child, with `governingAdrs` carrying what each ADR constrains *for that ticket* — including two traps a code-reading drafter cannot see (below). |
| No unvalidated assumption | ⚠️ | See concern 2. |

**Two traps deliberately written into the mémos** (a drafter reads code, not decision history):
1. **ADR-016 status-token collision.** `orders.status` already contains `refunded`, written by the
   *recovery runner* for a compensated **failed** checkout. A post-purchase refund of a **completed**
   order is a different fact. Reusing the token would make `classifyRecovered()` read a refunded
   completed order as a terminal checkout failure.
2. **ADR-021 append path.** Every lifecycle event must go through `store.appendLifecycle`; a direct
   INSERT reads as tampering to the verifier that runs inside `make check`.

**Concerns:**
1. **TKT-158 sizing** — likely to exceed the ~400-line review target. Accepted eyes-open; the plan
   gate is where the shape gets challenged.
2. **Fees, taxes and refund policy are out of scope everywhere** — TKT-6 (fees/splits) and TKT-32
   (VAT) do not exist yet, so every child refunds the *ticket price* only. When fees land, refund
   and cancellation policy (what is retained) will need a follow-up pass across all four. This is a
   known, named gap, not an oversight.
3. **Transfers and controlled resale are carved out to TKT-160**, not built. The epic's prose lists
   them; its Conditions of Success do not. They are blocked on an open product decision (*resale
   marketplace rules*, PRD open-decisions) and on TKT-21 (customer accounts) — the PRD itself names
   accounts as the prerequisite for transfers, and today's checkout is guest-only. TKT-9 will close
   on its three stated COS with that scope explicitly transferred, not silently dropped.

**COS coverage:**
| Epic COS | Covered by |
|---|---|
| Refund/exchange restore inventory and write compensating entries; chain still verifies | TKT-156 (money + compensating entry) + TKT-157 (inventory + tickets) + TKT-158 (exchange) |
| Exchanges settle price differences in either direction | TKT-158 |
| Cancellation flow processes an event's full order book with per-order outcomes | TKT-159 |

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — proceedable. The decomposition is sound and ordered; the named risks are
sizing on one child and a scope boundary (fees/policy, transfers/resale) that later epics own.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=claim -->
### ⚠️ Gateless run — the four human gates are waived for this epic

The repo owner has **deliberately waived all four human gates** for TKT-9 and its children as a
process experiment, and asked that the waiver be recorded on the board so the history shows this
work ran gateless. Recording it here, on the epic, so it is inherited-by-reference by every child.

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — priority (Backlog → Ready) | human transitions | **granted up front** by the owner |
| 2 — plan approval (Planning → Building) | human approves the plan | **agent self-resolves**: prefer the option the cross-model critique recommends; if it makes none, pick the most reversible. Every self-made decision + rationale is recorded in the `kind=plan-final` comment. |
| 3 — review + merge (Building → PO Review) | human reviews and squash-merges | **agent squash-merges** after the adversarial ai-review converges (same triage, second-pass and churn-cap rules). The review-guide is still posted first — it is the audit record. |
| 4 — PO acceptance (PO Review → Done) | PO validates | **agent self-validates** each COS against test evidence on the *merged* code, posts the validation note, then closes with the full metrics comment. |

**Unchanged and non-negotiable for this run:** `config.models` routing with no substitutions;
cross-model review for both plan and code; TDD with tests observed red first; `make check` green
before every push and after every merge; every marker comment posted at every stage; no AI
attribution anywhere in commits or PRs.

**Standing stop conditions** (report instead of proceeding): the gate or CI fails twice on the same
cause with no clear fix; the work would touch auth, money paths, data migrations or CI/deploy config
in a way the ticket and plan did not anticipate; a blocking review finding survives the churn cap;
a configured model is unreachable after the escalation ladder; or a destructive/irreversible action
with an ambiguous right answer.

Note on the second condition: this epic is **money by definition**, and every child says so in its
description and carries an explicit money-path warning. That is *anticipated* money work, which the
waiver covers. An **unanticipated** money-path surprise still stops the run.
